This first bail application has been filed by applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.255 of 2023 registered at Police Station Porsa, District Morena (M.P.) for offences punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376, 376(3),
506 of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in judicial custody since 09-10-2023.
As per the case of prosecution, mother of victim reported at PS Porsa, District Morena on 10-08-2023 that her daughter is missing since 11:00 AM on 10-08-2023.
She suspected that co-accused Gaurav Singh Tomar has allured and taken her daughter.
On such allegations, PS Porsa registered FIR at Crime No.255 of 2023 for offence punishable under Section 363 of IPC.

sentences.text: Initially, the victim refused to undergo medico-legal examination but later, on written request of her mother on 15-08-2023, the victim was medically examined.
In her initial statement recorded under Section 164 of CrPC on 12- 08-2023, the victim stated that she used to converse with Gaurav on mobile phone.
Her mother got angry, so her mother assaulted her, therefore, she left her parental home and went to Morena.
Around 05:00 in the evening, Gaurav came to her at Morena Bus-stand and informed her that her mother has lodged report against him, therefore, she should go back to her home.
She returned Porsa with Gaurav.
Both of them went directly to Police Station Porsa.
Gaurav has not committed any sexual assault on her.
She left her parental home on her own but returned on the advice of Gaurav.
In her second statement under Section 164 of CrPC recorded on 18-08- 2023, the victim alleged that Gaurav had committed rape on her near Morena Bus-stand.
She was threatened by Sneha and Kajal (applicant), therefore, she had not stated this fact in her earlier statement.

On such allegations,
offences punishable under Sections 366-A, 376, 376(3). 506 of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act were added.
The applicant was arrested on 09-10-2023.
She is in custody ever since.
Relevant recovery has been made.
Statement of witnesses have been recorded.

Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that it is a case of romantic relationship between two young persons i.e. the victim and co-accused Gaurav Singh Tomar.
The applicant is falsely implicated under pressure of family members of the victim after premeditation and delay of six days.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
The victim has alleged that she was threatened by Sneha and applicant Kajal.
Applicant Kajal is aged 18 years and Sneha is aged 16 years, therefore, the allegation is unbelievable.
The applicant is pursuing her study.
There is no likelihood of her absconding leaving behind her family and study.
Jail incarceration is causing hardship to the young applicant.
Investigation is almost complete, therefore, there is no likelihood of interfering with the investigation or tampering with the evidence.
The trial would take time to complete.
Therefore, the applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application and submits that the investigation is underway.
The applicant may not be extended the benefit of bail.
Heard learned learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, regard being had to the young age of applicant, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
